useWhen: Use CONTAINER when the source is an item that holds other items or coins: a backpack, sack, pouch, chest, quiver, case, bag of holding or portable hole. The items inside go under `CONTENTS`, each as its own Item.
notFor: The items inside the container. Each one is its own WEAPON, EQUIPMENT, CONSUMABLE, TOOL, LOOT or CONTAINER entry under `CONTENTS`.
A flask, vial or waterskin, where the liquid is the item: CONSUMABLE.
A worn item with no storage rules (belt, cloak): EQUIPMENT.
A spell that creates a storage space: SPELL.

checks: A container has no type key: `ITEM` holds `Name` and `Rarities`. `Container Type`, `USAGE` and `RECOVERY` are ignored with a warning, and a container never has `Activities`.

`CURRENCY_CONTENTS` needs all five keys (`Platinum`, `Gold`, `Electrum`, `Silver`, `Copper`) as whole numbers, with `0` for coins that are absent. A missing key fails. Leave the whole section out when there are no coins.

Write only the capacity limits the source gives and leave the other `CAPACITY` keys out. `0` gives a warning. Values are plain numbers: `500`, not `500 lb`. `CAPACITY.Volume Capacity Units` is `cubicFoot` or `liter`.
`COST_AND_WEIGHT.Weight Value` is the weight of the empty container. Do not add the contents.

Each `CONTENTS` entry is one full Item under exactly one root key: `WEAPON`, `EQUIPMENT`, `CONSUMABLE`, `TOOL`, `LOOT` or `CONTAINER`. Do not list bare names, do not repeat `SCHEMA_VERSION` inside an entry, and do not write `INVENTORY.Container` on a nested Item. Each of these fails.
A container always has quantity 1. A higher `INVENTORY.Quantity` is changed to 1 without a warning.

Set `PROPERTIES.Magical: true` on a magic container; `ATTUNEMENT.Attunement: required` does not set it. Always write `ITEM.Rarities` (`[]` for a mundane container; a missing key is stored as `common`) and `INVENTORY.Identified` (a missing key follows the user's setting).
